meta.label: English
meta.title: noaislop.xyz | your AI slop sucks.
meta.description: A page to send to someone who just published AI slop. Not about AI. About effort.
meta.ogDescription: Someone sent you this link. There’s a reason.
meta.ogImageAlt: The words “your AI slop sucks.” in green marker on an off-white background.

definition.text: Low-quality digital content, usually produced in quantity using artificial intelligence.
body: Not all AI content is slop. It becomes slop when nobody put any of themselves in it and it gets pushed on people who never asked.

dont.intro: It’s not the tool. It’s how you use it.
prompts: make me a flyer for my event
write me a motivational LinkedIn post about morning coffee
generate me a video of a cat saying have a good day
dont.lede: Ok you saved 3 minutes… but everyone who’ll see the result will suffer for it.
body: Every slop post buries something a person actually made. And once people spot slop in your work, they read everything you publish differently, including the good stuff.
Use AI to draft, to speed up the boring parts, to test an idea. Just put something of yours in what you publish.

example.prompt: vertical flyer. Photo I shot (attached) of last year’s venue as background, desaturated. Big condensed orange title, sans serif font, left-aligned, bottom third. Date and address in one line under the title.

blocks.title: Writing:
blocks.text: The idea is yours. Reread, rewritten, AI language tics removed. You can defend every claim in the text.

blocks.title: Images:
blocks.text: A real brief, references, a precise style. Not one line and the first generic output.

blocks.title: Video:
blocks.text: AI does a shot you couldn’t get, inside something you actually made.

items: Did you read all of it?
Is it free from that obvious AI look?
test.outro: Three yes: publish. Otherwise it’s slop.

emphasis: If you don’t put any of yourself into what you post, why should we bother reading it?

lines: Written by a human, reviewed by a human, defended by a human.
footer.note: Nobody’s saying you can’t create. We’d just like to see what **you** would have made.
